passages.text: For the law is only a shadow of the good things to come, not the realities themselves. It can never, by the same sacrifices offered year after year, make perfect those who draw near to worship.
passages.sermon:
The law is not the reality of good things to come.
The law is only a shadow of those good things.
The law is not the true image of what is coming.
People offer the same sacrifices every year under the law.
These sacrifices continue without end.
The law can never make those who come to worship perfect.
The law cannot make people perfect by these repeated sacrifices.
passages.original: Σκιὰν γὰρ ἔχων ὁ νόμος τῶν μελλόντων ἀγαθῶν οὐκ αὐτὴν τὴν εἰκόνα τῶν πραγμάτων κατ’ ἐνιαυτὸν ταῖς αὐταῖς θυσίαις ἃς προσφέρουσιν εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς οὐδέποτε δύναται τοὺς προσερχομένους τελειῶσαι

passages.text: If it could, would not the offerings have ceased? For the worshipers would have been cleansed once for all, and would no longer have felt the guilt of their sins.
passages.sermon:
The law required repeated sacrifices every year.
These sacrifices could not make people perfect.
If the sacrifices could make people perfect, they would have stopped.
The worshipers would have been cleansed once for all.
They would not feel guilty for their sins anymore.
passages.original: ἐπεὶ οὐκ ἂν ἐπαύσαντο προσφερόμεναι διὰ τὸ μηδεμίαν ἔχειν ἔτι συνείδησιν ἁμαρτιῶν τοὺς λατρεύοντας ἅπαξ κεκαθαρισμένους

passages.text: Instead, those sacrifices are an annual reminder of sins, because it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
passages.sermon:
The old sacrifices happen every year.
These sacrifices remind people of their sins each year.
The blood of bulls and goats cannot take away sins.
It is impossible for animal blood to remove sin.
passages.original: Ἀλλ’ ἐν αὐταῖς ἀνάμνησις ἁμαρτιῶν κατ’ ἐνιαυτόν ἀδύνατον γὰρ αἷμα ταύρων καὶ τράγων ἀφαιρεῖν ἁμαρτίας

passages.text: Therefore, when Christ came into the world, He said: “Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but a body You prepared for Me.
passages.sermon:
Christ came into the world.
Christ spoke to God.
God did not want sacrifice.
God did not want offering.
God prepared a body for Christ.
passages.original: Διὸ εἰσερχόμενος εἰς τὸν κόσμον λέγει Θυσίαν καὶ προσφορὰν οὐκ ἠθέλησας Σῶμα δὲ κατηρτίσω μοι

passages.text: In burnt offerings and sin offerings You took no delight.
passages.sermon: God did not delight in burnt offerings.\r\nGod did not delight in sin offerings.
passages.original: Ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας Οὐκ εὐδόκησας

passages.text: Then I said, ‘Here I am, it is written about Me in the scroll: I have come to do Your will, O God.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Christ spoke these words when He came into the world.
He said, “Here I am.”
The scroll contains words written about Me.
I have come to do Your will, O God.
God, I am ready to obey You.
My purpose is to fulfill what is written about Me.
I will do what You desire.
passages.original: Τότε εἶπον Ἰδοὺ ἥκω Ἐν κεφαλίδι βιβλίου γέγραπται περὶ ἐμοῦ Τοῦ ποιῆσαι ὁ Θεός τὸ θέλημά σου

passages.text: In the passage above He says, “Sacrifices and offerings, burnt offerings and sin offerings You did not desire, nor did You delight in them” (although they are offered according to the law).
passages.sermon:
God spoke in the passage above.
God said, “I did not desire sacrifices and offerings.
I did not desire burnt offerings and sin offerings.
I did not delight in them.
People offer these sacrifices according to the law.
But I did not want them.”
passages.original: Ἀνώτερον λέγων ὅτι Θυσίας καὶ προσφορὰς καὶ ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας οὐκ ἠθέλησας οὐδὲ εὐδόκησας αἵτινες κατὰ νόμον προσφέρονται

passages.text: Then He adds, “Here I am, I have come to do Your will.” He takes away the first to establish the second.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks.
He says, "Here I am."
Jesus says, "I have come to do Your will."
God removes the first way.
God does this to establish the second way.
passages.original: τότε εἴρηκεν Ἰδοὺ ἥκω τοῦ ποιῆσαι τὸ θέλημά σου ἀναιρεῖ τὸ πρῶτον ἵνα τὸ δεύτερον στήσῃ

passages.text: And by that will, we have been sanctified through the sacrifice of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
passages.sermon:
God has a will.
God’s will is for us to be made holy.
Jesus Christ offered His body as a sacrifice.
Jesus sacrificed Himself once for all people.
God’s will made us holy through Jesus’ sacrifice.
passages.original: ἐν ᾧ θελήματι ἡγιασμένοι ἐσμὲν διὰ τῆς προσφορᾶς τοῦ σώματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐφάπαξ

passages.text: Day after day every priest stands to minister and to offer again and again the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.
passages.sermon:
Every priest serves God.
Each priest stands every day.
Each priest performs his duties every day.
Each priest offers the same sacrifices many times.
These sacrifices cannot remove sins.
No sacrifice offered by these priests can ever take away sins.
passages.original: Καὶ πᾶς μὲν ἱερεὺς ἕστηκεν καθ’ ἡμέραν λειτουργῶν καὶ τὰς αὐτὰς πολλάκις προσφέρων θυσίας αἵτινες οὐδέποτε δύνανται περιελεῖν ἁμαρτίας

passages.text: But when this Priest had offered for all time one sacrifice for sins, He sat down at the right hand of God.
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ is the Priest.
He offered one sacrifice for sins.
This sacrifice was for all time.
After He offered this sacrifice, He sat down.
He sat at the right hand of God.
passages.original: οὗτος δὲ μίαν ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτιῶν προσενέγκας θυσίαν εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς ἐκάθισεν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Since that time, He waits for His enemies to be made a footstool for His feet, because by a single offering He has made perfect for all time those who are being sanctified.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the great High Priest.
He offered one sacrifice for sins.
He now sits at the right hand of God.
Since that time, Jesus waits.
He waits until God makes His enemies a footstool for His feet.
By one offering, Jesus made perfect forever those who are being sanctified.
He made holy all who are being made holy.
passages.original: τὸ λοιπὸν ἐκδεχόμενος ἕως τεθῶσιν οἱ ἐχθροὶ αὐτοῦ ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ μιᾷ γὰρ προσφορᾷ τετελείωκεν εἰς τὸ διηνεκὲς τοὺς ἁγιαζομένους

passages.text: The Holy Spirit also testifies to us about this. First He says: “This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, declares the Lord. I will put My laws in their hearts and inscribe them on their minds.”
passages.sermon:
The Holy Spirit testifies to us.
The Holy Spirit speaks about this matter.
The Lord says, “This is the covenant I will make with them after those days.”
The Lord declares this promise.
The Lord says, “I will put My laws in their hearts.”
The Lord says, “I will write My laws on their minds.”
passages.original: Μαρτυρεῖ δὲ ἡμῖν καὶ τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον μετὰ γὰρ τὸ εἰρηκέναι Αὕτη ἡ διαθήκη ἣν διαθήσομαι πρὸς αὐτοὺς μετὰ τὰς ἡμέρας ἐκείνας λέγει Κύριος διδοὺς νόμους μου ἐπὶ καρδίας αὐτῶν καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν διάνοιαν αὐτῶν ἐπιγράψω αὐτούς

passages.text: Then He adds: “Their sins and lawless acts I will remember no more.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks.
God says something new.
God says, “I will not remember their sins.”
God says, “I will not remember their lawless acts.”
God will never remember these things again.
passages.original: Καὶ Τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν καὶ τῶν ἀνομιῶν αὐτῶν οὐ μὴ μνησθήσομαι ἔτι

passages.text: And where these have been forgiven, an offering for sin is no longer needed.
passages.sermon: God forgives these sins.\r\nWhere God forgives sins, no more offering for sin is needed.\r\nNo one needs to bring another sacrifice for sin.
passages.original: Ὅπου δὲ ἄφεσις τούτων οὐκέτι προσφορὰ περὶ ἁμαρτίας

passages.text: Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence to enter the Most Holy Place by the blood of Jesus, by the new and living way opened for us through the curtain of His body, and since we have a great priest over the house of God, let us draw near with a sincere heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled to cleanse us from a guilty conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
passages.sermon:
Brothers, we have confidence.
We can enter the Most Holy Place.
We enter by the blood of Jesus.
Jesus opened a new and living way for us.
He opened this way through the curtain.
The curtain means His body.
We have a great priest over the house of God.
Let us draw near to God.
Let us come with a sincere heart.
Let us have full assurance of faith.
Our hearts are sprinkled clean.
We are cleansed from a guilty conscience.
Our bodies are washed with pure water.
passages.original: Ἔχοντες οὖν ἀδελφοί παρρησίαν εἰς τὴν εἴσοδον τῶν ἁγίων ἐν τῷ αἵματι Ἰησοῦ ἣν ἐνεκαίνισεν ἡμῖν ὁδὸν πρόσφατον καὶ ζῶσαν διὰ τοῦ καταπετάσματος τοῦτ’ ἔστιν τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἱερέα μέγαν ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Θεοῦ προσερχώμεθα μετὰ ἀληθινῆς καρδίας ἐν πληροφορίᾳ πίστεως ῥεραντισμένοι τὰς καρδίας ἀπὸ συνειδήσεως πονηρᾶς καὶ λελουσμένοι τὸ σῶμα ὕδατι καθαρῷ

passages.text: Let us hold resolutely to the hope we profess, for He who promised is faithful.
passages.sermon:
God made a promise to us.
God is faithful.
We profess hope in God’s promise.
Let us hold firmly to this hope.
Let us not waver.
passages.original: Κατέχωμεν τὴν ὁμολογίαν τῆς ἐλπίδος ἀκλινῆ πιστὸς γὰρ ὁ ἐπαγγειλάμενος

passages.text: And let us consider how to spur one another on to love and good deeds.
passages.sermon:
We are brothers and sisters in Christ.
We follow Jesus.
Let us think about each other.
Let us help each other do loving things.
Let us encourage each other to do good deeds.
passages.original: καὶ κατανοῶμεν ἀλλήλους εἰς παροξυσμὸν ἀγάπης καὶ καλῶν ἔργων

passages.text: Let us not neglect meeting together, as some have made a habit, but let us encourage one another, and all the more as you see the Day approaching.
passages.sermon:
We are followers of Jesus Christ.
Some people have stopped meeting together.
Let us not neglect meeting together.
Let us encourage one another.
Let us encourage each other even more as we see the Day of the Lord coming closer.
passages.original: μὴ ἐγκαταλείποντες τὴν ἐπισυναγωγὴν ἑαυτῶν καθὼς ἔθος τισίν ἀλλὰ παρακαλοῦντες καὶ τοσούτῳ μᾶλλον ὅσῳ βλέπετε ἐγγίζουσαν τὴν ἡμέραν

passages.text: If we deliberately go on sinning after we have received the knowledge of the truth, no further sacrifice for sins remains, but only a fearful expectation of judgment and of raging fire that will consume all adversaries.
passages.sermon:
We have received the knowledge of the truth.
We know what is right.
If we deliberately keep on sinning after this,
there is no sacrifice left for our sins.
There is nothing else that can take away our sins.
Instead, we can only expect judgment.
We can only wait in fear for what will come.
A raging fire will come.
This fire will consume all who oppose God.
passages.original: Ἑκουσίως γὰρ ἁμαρτανόντων ἡμῶν μετὰ τὸ λαβεῖν τὴν ἐπίγνωσιν τῆς ἀληθείας οὐκέτι περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν ἀπολείπεται θυσία φοβερὰ δέ τις ἐκδοχὴ κρίσεως καὶ πυρὸς ζῆλος ἐσθίειν μέλλοντος τοὺς ὑπεναντίους

passages.text: Anyone who rejected the law of Moses died without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
passages.sermon:
Moses gave the law to the people of Israel.
Some people rejected this law.
If a person rejected the law of Moses, he faced judgment.
Two or three witnesses could testify against him.
If the witnesses agreed, the person died.
He received no mercy.
passages.original: ἀθετήσας τις νόμον Μωϋσέως χωρὶς οἰκτιρμῶν ἐπὶ δυσὶν ἢ τρισὶν μάρτυσιν ἀποθνήσκει

passages.text: How much more severely do you think one deserves to be punished who has trampled on the Son of God, profaned the blood of the covenant that sanctified him, and insulted the Spirit of grace?
passages.sermon:
This passage speaks about people who reject Jesus Christ after knowing the truth.
Jesus Christ is the Son of God.
Some people trample on the Son of God.
They treat the blood of the covenant as something common.
This blood made them holy.
They insult the Spirit of grace.
Such people deserve much greater punishment.
Their punishment will be more severe than those who rejected the law of Moses.
passages.original: πόσῳ δοκεῖτε χείρονος ἀξιωθήσεται τιμωρίας ὁ τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ καταπατήσας καὶ τὸ αἷμα τῆς διαθήκης κοινὸν ἡγησάμενος ἐν ᾧ ἡγιάσθη καὶ τὸ Πνεῦμα τῆς χάριτος ἐνυβρίσας

passages.text: For we know Him who said, “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay,” and again, “The Lord will judge His people.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke these words.
God said, “Vengeance is Mine. I will repay.”
God also said, “The Lord will judge His people.”
We know the One who said these things.
passages.original: Οἴδαμεν γὰρ τὸν εἰπόντα Ἐμοὶ ἐκδίκησις ἐγὼ ἀνταποδώσω καὶ πάλιν Κρινεῖ Κύριος τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
passages.sermon:
God is living.
God has power.
Falling into God's hands brings fear.
It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
passages.original: φοβερὸν τὸ ἐμπεσεῖν εἰς χεῖρας Θεοῦ ζῶντος

passages.text: Remember the early days that you were in the light. In those days, you endured a great conflict in the face of suffering.
passages.sermon:
You are believers in Jesus Christ.
You once received the light of the gospel.
Remember those early days.
In those days, you suffered much.
You faced a great struggle.
You endured many hardships.
passages.original: Ἀναμιμνῄσκεσθε δὲ τὰς πρότερον ἡμέρας ἐν αἷς φωτισθέντες πολλὴν ἄθλησιν ὑπεμείνατε παθημάτων

passages.text: Sometimes you were publicly exposed to ridicule and persecution; at other times you were partners with those who were so treated.
passages.sermon:
You are believers in Jesus Christ.
You sometimes suffered public ridicule.
You sometimes faced persecution.
At other times, you joined with others who suffered the same way.
You became partners with those who were mistreated.
passages.original: τοῦτο μὲν ὀνειδισμοῖς τε καὶ θλίψεσιν θεατριζόμενοι τοῦτο δὲ κοινωνοὶ τῶν οὕτως ἀναστρεφομένων γενηθέντες

passages.text: You sympathized with those in prison and joyfully accepted the confiscation of your property, knowing that you yourselves had a better and permanent possession.
passages.sermon:
You showed sympathy to people in prison.
You felt compassion for them.
You accepted the loss of your property with joy.
You knew you had something better.
You understood your possession is greater and will last forever.
passages.original: καὶ γὰρ τοῖς δεσμίοις συνεπαθήσατε καὶ τὴν ἁρπαγὴν τῶν ὑπαρχόντων ὑμῶν μετὰ χαρᾶς προσεδέξασθε γινώσκοντες ἔχειν ἑαυτοὺς κρείττονα ὕπαρξιν καὶ μένουσαν

passages.text: So do not throw away your confidence; it holds a great reward.
passages.sermon:
You have confidence.
This confidence is important.
Do not throw away your confidence.
Your confidence brings a great reward.
passages.original: Μὴ ἀποβάλητε οὖν τὴν παρρησίαν ὑμῶν ἥτις ἔχει μεγάλην μισθαποδοσίαν

passages.text: You need to persevere, so that after you have done the will of God, you will receive what He has promised.
passages.sermon:
You need perseverance.
Perseverance means you keep going.
You must do the will of God.
When you do God’s will, you will receive what God has promised.
God’s promise is for those who persevere and obey Him.
passages.original: ὑπομονῆς γὰρ ἔχετε χρείαν ἵνα τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Θεοῦ ποιήσαντες κομίσησθε τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν

passages.text: For, “In just a little while, He who is coming will come and will not delay.
passages.sermon: Jesus is coming soon.\r\nHe will not delay.\r\nHe will arrive in a little while.
passages.original: ἔτι γὰρ Μικρὸν ὅσον ὅσον ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἥξει καὶ οὐ χρονίσει

passages.text: But My righteous one will live by faith; and if he shrinks back, I will take no pleasure in him.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His righteous one.
God calls this person "My righteous one."
God says, "My righteous one will live by faith."
God also says, "If he shrinks back, I will not be pleased with him."
passages.original: ὁ δὲ δίκαιός μου ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται καὶ ἐὰν ὑποστείληται οὐκ εὐδοκεῖ ἡ ψυχή μου ἐν αὐτῷ

passages.text: But we are not of those who shrink back and are destroyed, but of those who have faith and preserve their souls.
passages.sermon:
We are not people who shrink back.
We do not turn away from God.
We do not end in destruction.
We are people who have faith.
We trust God.
We keep our souls safe by faith.
passages.original: Ἡμεῖς δὲ οὐκ ἐσμὲν ὑποστολῆς εἰς ἀπώλειαν ἀλλὰ πίστεως εἰς περιποίησιν ψυχῆς
